cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the situation ahead has not declared what it is.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Say the true thing you've been quietly noticing about a situation that hasn't settled — out loud, to the person it concerns — then let their response stand without smoothing it.
cells.core: You can hold something clearly while it's still deciding what it is. That isn't delay. You stand beside a half-formed situation and see it quite precisely, and you don't rush to name what it means, because naming it too early would make it smaller than it is. That precision is running right now, without your supervision, the way it does. What's useful to know is that clear sight has a lifespan. A situation stays openable for a while, and after that the reading is accurate but useless, because nobody can act on it anymore. The thing you're watching waits to be named by someone who has actually looked. You've looked. Saying it plainly, to one person, before the moment closes, is the same seeing doing its second half.
cells.sheetLine: You see what a thing is before it has decided, and that isn't delay.
cells.verb: seeing clearly what has not yet taken shape, and speaking it when it can be heard
cells.place: the open ground before anything has been decided

cells.tense: You are braced for how this turns out, before it has had a chance to turn.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Take the thing you keep pushing forward and move at its pace — do today's share, nothing toward next week, until the stretch ends by itself.
cells.core: Your read arrives faster than the thing it's reading. A situation in its first days gets understood almost instantly, and you're already at the plan, the right word, the finished version — all before the situation has said anything back. The read is good. The speed has carried you past the part where you'd find out if it's true. What you're tending is being prepared for a future that hasn't been agreed to, and from the inside it feels like care. Attending to what might happen gives what's here no room. Work at the pace the thing itself sets. Don't perfect the plan for it. Stay with it long enough that it shows you something you hadn't already decided.
cells.sheetLine: You've already arrived at how it ends.
cells.verb: seeing clearly what has not yet taken shape, and speaking it when it can be heard

cells.tense: There was a moment to say the true thing, and you are still standing at it, after.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Stay close to a person who's struggling, quiet, fixing nothing, explaining nothing — and step away once you've given what you have.
cells.core: The clarity hasn't left you, but it's gone quiet, and the fast read of a room that used to arrive without effort isn't arriving. You've stopped saying what you actually see, and somewhere in that you stopped expecting to be asked. Things stay unread because you're not looking, and you're not looking because at some point looking stopped seeming to matter to anyone. Here's the smaller door back in: sit with one person's feeling without correcting it or shrinking it to something manageable. You don't need to be right about what they feel. You don't need the words. Stay with them in it for as long as you have, with your own feet under you, and stop there.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped saying what you see, and stopped expecting to be asked.

cells.tense: You are reading the room accurately right now and calling the reading just how things are.
cells.act: make a ritual of the shared thing
cells.ask: Take what you and your people already do together and make it named and regular — same shape, same time — and say out loud that you set it that way.
cells.core: You are already doing this — the read, the measured word, the timing of when to speak — and you have been filing it under circumstance. You say the room happened to be ready, or anyone would have noticed, or it was just the obvious move. That isn't what's happening. The clarity is yours, and the judgment about when the truth can land is yours, and you keep speaking from a place you won't sign. This matters here, on ground where nothing has shapes yet: somebody has to say what's real first, and you keep being that somebody. Take what you already do with your people — the way you mark a hard week — do it deliberately, on a day you chose, and say you chose it.
cells.sheetLine: The read and the timing are yours, filed under circumstance.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's steadiness has already been picked up by others or that people lean on them without being told to — the record names the seat and the mechanism but not what anyone else is doing. A reader could reasonably say the weight they carry is being read into, and if that read is wrong the ask still holds because holding a moment open without ruling on it is useful regardless of anyone else's response. The sentence that serves me more than them is the closing move in the Balanced core about steadiness being seen — it's the likely candidate and I've kept it inside the mechanism rather than the person's history.
